text:
maria: Heads-up: seeing steady KV cache page-table growth on longctx tests with paged attention on RTX6000. H100 run doesn't show the same leak. Repro steps + perf traces below.
kevin: Can you paste the perf summary and the exact repro command? still thinking remap atomicity vs eviction ordering.
maria: Perf snapshot (RTX6000):
```
pt_entries=+512 every 1024 tokens
kv_pages_alloc=2048 -> 3680 over 25k tokens
evicted_pages=1200
evict_free_attempts=1200
leaked_slots=msvc_stub: 0x7f3a... (not freed)
```
Run: ./tools/longctx_repro --model llama-7b --tokens 25000 --gpu rtx6000 --batch-size 16
anil: Is this deterministic? Could driver memcopy alignment or different PCIe ordering be leaving a stale owner bit? Also check eviction order under batching.
maria: Deterministic: I repeated 5x on same node. H100 run shows pt_entries plateau after ~8k tokens; RTX6000 keeps growing. Heaptrace snippet shows pt holecount rising.

```
heap: pt_slot[12345] state=assigned owner=0x11 key=... refcnt=0
pt_slot[12346] state=evicted owner=0x0 refcnt=1
```

Looks like eviction marks but refcnt remains >0.
dana: Hypothesis: our remap path assumes write-after-write ordering that's only guaranteed on H100 but not older driver/arch. Try adding an smp_store_release / cudaStreamSynchronize pair after remap to enforce ordering.
kevin: Quick experiment idea: add a memory_fence() after pt->owner updates and before eviction unmap. Patch snippet:
```
// pseudo
atomic_store_explicit(&pt->owner, new_owner, memory_order_release);
__sync_synchronize(); // or cudaDeviceSynchronize in repro
```
Also check batching: larger batch windows mean larger KV live sets -> increases chance to hit the race.
infra-bot: CI: longctx-repro (rtx6000) queued by maria
todd: Can we run with continuous-batching=off and with kv-eviction-threshold=0.6 to see if it's batching-related? If slope drops it's likely reuse window interaction.
maria: Ran with fencing patch: leak slope reduced ~90% (kv_pages_alloc from +1632 -> +180 over 25k tokens). H100 unaffected as expected. So ordering bug seems real.
kevin: Nice. Please open a minimal PR and add the fencing as optional behind an arch-guard. Perf overhead should be tiny (<1% token throughput in my quick runs).
anil: Also add a microbenchmark to perf suite that concurrently remaps and evicts across 8 threads to catch regressions.
maria: Will open PR 9424 and add the test under eng-runtime/perf/kv_repro. Pushing logs and raw perf CSV to the thread in a minute. cc @kevin @anil @dana :thumbsup:
kevin: Great. After PR we should run Dedicated canary. Also add a note in changelog about platform-specific pager fences.
dana: Agree; file a follow-up to audit other places where we rely on implicit write ordering.
maria: Thanks all — I'll own the PR and next steps. Closing the loop once canary is green. :white_check_mark:
